surfaces: Standalone terminal agent published as npm @github/copilot (bin name `copilot` -> `copilot.exe` on Windows) with per-platform native packages @github/copilot-win32-x64 / -win32-arm64 / -linux-x64 / -darwin-x64. The npm wrapper only spawns the native binary; the real implementation ships inside the platform package as a Node SEA (node:sea) that embeds `copilot.tgz` and extracts it to a pkg cache. The extracted package contains cli-main.js (8.2 MB bundle), app.js, index.js, prebuilds/win32-x64/runtime.node (122 MB Rust napi runtime = the agent harness), schemas/session-events.schema.json (1 MB, 196 event types), schemas/api.schema.json, copilot-sdk/ (public SDK + docs), definitions/*.agent.yaml, plugins/, builtin-skills/. A separate Rust helper `copilot-taskbar-activator.exe` handles Windows taskbar integration. The agent is the same harness as GitHub's Copilot coding agent: local session with tool calls, subagents, MCP servers, skills, permissions, plan/checkpoints, and a resumable local session store. The Rust runtime source lives in github/copilot-agent-runtime, which is NOT publicly readable (raw.githubusercontent 404, referenced only by upstream PR links inside changelog.json), so the npm artifact is the authoritative upstream source.
binaries: npm: `@github/copilot` (latest 1.0.101, bin `copilot` -> npm-loader.js) + optionalDependencies `@github/copilot-<platform>-<arch>` (native binary `copilot.exe` on Windows, 170 MB). Also distributed via winget (repo has .github/workflows/winget.yml) and GitHub releases of github/copilot-cli (install.sh).

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.copilot  (Copilot home; upstream `resolveCopilotHome(null,null,"C:\\Users\\PC")` -> `C:\Users\PC\.copilot`; overridable via COPILOT_HOME env var)
%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-state\<sessionId>\  (session workspace: plan.md, client-metadata.json, checkpoints\, files\, research\, per-session SQLite db)

%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-store.db  (local SQLite history across sessions: tables sessions(id,cwd,repository,host_type,branch,summary,created_at,updated_at), turns, checkpoints, session_files, session_refs, assistant_usage_events, search_index; note: no tool_executions/events tables locally)
%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-state\<sessionId>.jsonl  (LEGACY flat per-session file, pre-1.0 layout; upstream `hasLegacyFlatSessionFile`)
storage.format: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), one SessionEvent object per line. Verified by running the shipped native module: the upstream loader error text is "Failed to read JSONL from ...\events.jsonl: Invalid event at line 1: invalid session event envelope: `id` must be a UUID string." Envelope = {id: UUID v4, timestamp: ISO-8601, parentId: UUID|null (linked chain), ephemeral?: bool, agentId?: string, type: string, data: {...}}. 196 event types are defined in schemas/session-events.schema.json (session.start, tool.execution_start/complete, assistant.turn_start/turn_end/reasoning, session.model_change, session.task_complete, subagent.started, session.idle, session.shutdown, user.message, assistant.message, ...). Not encrypted, not a proprietary binary DB, not SQLite for the event log.
storage.append_semantics: LIVE APPEND during the run (not rewritten at the end). Upstream writer API `sessionEventsAppendToFsJson(jsonArray, sessionId, sessionStatePath, conventions)` appends to the JSONL file (error text: "Failed to append to JSONL file ..."). The CLI registers a per-session background writer (`sessionEventWriterEnsureRegistered` + `sessionEventWriterSetFlushDebounce(ms)` + `sessionEventWriterFlush`, flushDebounceMs is a CLI option) and calls flushPendingWrites on save, so events land on disk while the agent works. Verified end-to-end: I appended two events through the shipped runtime into a sandbox dir and read back exactly two newline-terminated lines. Events marked `"ephemeral": true` are explicitly NOT persisted ("the event is transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk").
storage.session_file_naming: Current: <sessionsHome>\<sessionId>\events.jsonl. Legacy: <sessionsHome>\<sessionId>.jsonl. sessionId is a UUID-style string (schema requires event `id` to be a UUID; session dir name equals the sessionId emitted in session.start.data.sessionId).

fields.project: YES - session.start.data.context.cwd (WorkingDirectoryContext.cwd, absolute workspace path) plus gitRoot, repository ("owner/name"), branch, headCommit. Also persisted per session in workspace.yaml.
fields.model: YES - session.start.data.selectedModel (+providerId), tool.execution_start.data.model, assistant.turn_start.data.model, session.model_change.data.newModel / previousModel.
fields.file_basename: YES - tool.execution_start.data.arguments.path is the absolute path for the file tools (view / create / edit / str_replace / insert / apply_patch / str_replace_editor); tool.execution_complete.data.fileEdits[] carries absolute edited paths (experimental). Only the basename may be published.
fields.tool_activity: YES - tool.execution_start.data.toolName + toolCallId (+ shellToolInfo for shell path hints); tool.execution_complete.data.success/error/result. Built-in tool names found upstream: view, create, edit, str_replace, insert, apply_patch, str_replace_editor, local_shell, bash, grep, rg, glob, ask_user, task, list_agents, read_agent, write_agent, skill, sql, session_store_sql, lexical_code_search, semantic_code_search, execution_subagent.
fields.phase: YES - assistant.turn_start / assistant.turn_end delimit the agent loop turn; assistant.reasoning marks thinking; session.idle, session.task_complete and session.shutdown mark turn/session completion. subagent.started marks a sub-agent spawn.
fields.timestamps: YES - envelope.timestamp is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds (e.g. "2026-10-21T02:00:03.500Z"); session.start.data.startTime is ISO-8601; events are ordered and chained via parentId.

parser_strategy:
One JSON object per line, so the existing LogTailer works unchanged. New fn parse_copilot_cli_line(line) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>; dispatch on value["type"] inside value["data"]:

- "session.start": data.context.cwd (fallback data.context.gitRoot, then data.context.workingDirectory) -> SessionMetadata{project: project_name(cwd), cwd}; data.startTime (fallback envelope timestamp) -> TaskStarted{started_at_ms}; data.selectedModel -> AgentDetected{agent: model_id(data.selectedModel)}.
- "assistant.turn_start": envelope timestamp -> TaskStarted{started_at_ms} (per-turn elapsed timer); data.model -> AgentDetected (only if it differs from the last seen model).
- "assistant.reasoning": -> Thinking{reasoning: None} (never the reasoning text).
- "tool.execution_start": needs data.toolName + data.toolCallId -> TrackedToolStarted{call_id: data.toolCallId, activity: ToolActivity{label: classify_tool(toolName.to_lowercase(), args.command), file: extract_file_basename(data.arguments), language: language_from_file(file)}}. Copilot's file tools use the "path" key, so the existing extract_file_basename already finds it; apply_patch is covered by the existing "patch"/"*** Update File:" branch.
- "tool.execution_complete": data.toolCallId -> TrackedToolFinished{call_id}.
- "session.model_change": data.newModel -> AgentDetected{agent: model_id(...)} (validated charset, <=128 chars, like deepseek_model_label).
- "subagent.started": data.agentDisplayName/data.agentName -> AgentDetected{agent}; optionally SubagentSpawned{conversation_id: data.toolCallId, agent: data.agentName}.
- "session.task_complete" | "assistant.turn_end" | "session.idle" | "session.shutdown": -> Completed.
- Everything else (user.message, assistant.message, permission.*, hook.*, ...): ignored. Never read data.content, data.summary, data.result, data.error, data.arguments values other than the path basename, or the raw command string.

Hard privacy rule for this provider: model ids and file basenames are the ONLY free-form strings allowed out of a line; label strings come from the fixed classify_tool table.

risks: Executable-name collision: the GitHub Copilot CLI installs `copilot.exe`, which Discodex currently maps to Provider::MicrosoftCopilot. Re-pointing bare "copilot" to the new variant can break detection of the Microsoft Copilot consumer app (also a Copilot.exe). Resolve by full install path (Microsoft Store Apps folder) instead of file name, and update the from_executable unit test.

Path/layout is an internal implementation detail ("session-state", "events.jsonl") of a closed-source Rust runtime; it is referenced in the shipped SDK docs but is not a stable public API and can change between CLI releases. Fail safe by keeping focused-app detection as a fallback and by logging when the root is missing.

Format churn: the runtime validates session events strictly (envelope id must be a UUID) and the schema is versioned; new event types and renamed data fields will appear. The parser must ignore unknown types/fields and never abort a log file on one bad line.

Privacy: events.jsonl contains the full conversation - user prompts, assistant replies, tool arguments and tool results. The adapter must only ever read envelope.type, data.toolName, data.toolCallId, data.selectedModel/newModel, data.context.cwd and the `path` key of data.arguments; every other field must be dropped unread. A regression test asserting no prompt/result text can reach a ToolActivity label, file, or agent string is mandatory.

Full-path leakage: data.arguments.path and data.fileEdits[] are absolute paths. Only the basename may be published; the cwd must be reduced to the final folder name (project_name()) and never sent as a path.

Replay cost: read_from_start() at startup replays entire session histories (potentially 10s of thousands of lines per session). Bound the startup replay for this provider (tail-only or time-windowed) to avoid CPU spikes and stale state.

Local-only: cloud/remote Copilot sessions (agent hosted by GitHub) write no local events.jsonl, so the adapter will not track them - acceptable, but the focused detection path should still cover the terminal window.

The session dir also holds a per-session SQLite db and the global session-store.db; do not attempt to parse them (would need a new sqlite dependency for marginal gain) - the JSONL already carries everything needed.
confidence: high for storage format, exact paths and append semantics (each verified by executing the shipped upstream native module and by the upstream loader/writer error strings and the SDK docs shipped in the same package); medium for cross-version stability of the directory/file names and for the exact tool-argument keys of every built-in tool (verified for the file tools via SDK examples and the CLI's own zod schemas, not exhaustively for all tools).
summary: GitHub Copilot CLI (npm @github/copilot, native `copilot.exe`) writes a LOCAL, APPEND-ONLY, NEWLINE-DELIMITED JSON session event log at %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-state\<sessionId>\events.jsonl, written live by a debounced background writer while the agent works. One JSON object per line, envelope {id(UUID),timestamp(ISO-8601 ms),parentId,ephemeral,agentId,type,data}, 196 documented event types (schemas/session-events.schema.json). It carries everything Discodex needs without exposing conversation text: session.start.data.context.cwd (project), session.start.data.selectedModel / session.model_change.data.newModel (model), tool.execution_start.data.toolName + toolCallId + arguments.path (normalized tool activity + file basename), assistant.turn_start/turn_end + assistant.reasoning (phase), session.start.data.startTime (timer). No auth token, no encryption, no proprietary binary DB, no SQLite requirement. The main integration risk is a name collision: `copilot.exe` currently maps to Provider::MicrosoftCopilot, and the repo already has a GitHubCopilot variant for the IDE extension, so a new Provider::CopilotCli variant is required. Verdict: rich.
